Quick answers / immediate asks: 

- What we can produce: per-request access logs (timestamp, request_id, model_id, route, latency_ms, status_code), service trace spans (sampled at 10% by default), and the KV-cache hit/miss counters. Full request/response bodies are only retained for a short window and are subject to customer opt-in; default truncation/redaction removes sensitive fields.

- Retention: access logs (non-body) retained 90 days in the hot S3 bucket; sampled traces retained 30 days; request/response bodies (if captured) are retained for 7 days and archived separately for customers with extended retention.

- Chain-of-custody: exports are generated via a signed job (internal job id) that writes to a secured S3 export bucket; job metadata includes operator, timestamp, and SHA256 of the archive — we can provide that job id and the archive checksum for the export.

Action items I need from Stephanie/infra: 
1) Run an export for brightbank account id BRB-114 for the window 2027-04-27T20:00:00Z–2027-04-27T20:30:00Z (their local 16:00–16:30 ET). Include per-request log lines and sampled trace spans.
2) Confirm whether any request bodies were captured for that account in that window and whether they were redacted.

I'll prep a short one-slide summary for the execs once we have the export checksum.

—Sean
Director, Runtime Reliability
